items.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: When you think of Thelonious Monk, for good, bad or otherwise, Monk was always Monk, whether it was profitable for him or not.

ctx.x: Slam Stewart and Oscar Pettiford. And Ray has told me stories about going to watch Oscar Pettiford play and just being the wide-eyed kid in the front row. And we take in everything that we hear. I mean I’m sure there’s a good bit of Barbara Mandrell and Anne Murray and Tom T. Hall inside of me. You know? I mean just because that’s part of my upbringing. It’s part of what I know. But I think ultimately our job as musicians is to tell our story in whatever way that is. And that’s an intangible. Because everybody is…
That was such a big part of that era of the music is people having their own identifiable sound.
